image_description: A night-time photograph showing a woman holding a hammerhead shark vertically by its cephalofoil (head). The shark's ventral side (white belly) is facing the camera. In the background, two men are visible, one shirtless and one in a uniform, along with a blue cooler. The lighting is harsh, likely from an on-camera flash.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the laterally expanded, dorsoventrally flattened cephalofoil (hammer-shaped head).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The subject clearly displays the iconic T-shaped head structure characteristic of hammerhead sharks.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned at the extreme lateral tips of the cephalofoil.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image shows the ventral (underbelly) view of the shark. Eyes are located on the dorsal (top) surface of the cephalofoil and are completely occluded from this angle.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned near the lateral margins of the cephalofoil.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Small dark spots consistent with nostril placement are visible on the underside of the hammer-head wings.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Anterior margin of the cephalofoil is straight to slightly curved with a central indentation in some species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The leading edge of the head is visible and appears structurally sound with a slight central curve/indentation typical of the species.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is streamlined and laterally compressed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Despite being held vertically, the body tapers correctly towards the tail, indicating a streamlined shape.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dorsal coloration is grey to brownish with white ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible ventral side is white/light grey, transitioning to darker grey on the sides, matching the countershading description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is covered in dermal denticles with a rough texture.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Image resolution and harsh flash lighting prevent microscopic verification of dermal denticles; skin appears smooth due to specular highlights.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: First dorsal fin is tall and falcate (sickle-shaped), positioned anteriorly.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal fin is on the top of the shark and is occluded by the body in this ventral-up hold position.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Pectoral fins are broad and triangular.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Both pectoral fins are clearly visible, extending laterally with the correct triangular morphology.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caudal fin is asymmetrical with a pronounced upper lobe.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail fin is visible at the bottom; while partially obscured by the angle, the heterocercal (asymmetrical) nature is discernible.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The skin texture appears unusually smooth and plastic-like in the center of the belly, lacking the expected subtle granularity of shark skin, though this may be exacerbated by flash overexposure.

artifact_observations.location: Junction of right pectoral fin and body
artifact_observations.reasoning: The connection point of the right pectoral fin (viewer's left) to the body appears slightly soft and indistinct, lacking a sharp anatomical boundary, suggesting minor generation blur or fusion.

To verify the anatomical correctness of the fins and tail despite the unnatural vertical holding pose.
To analyze the impact of harsh flash lighting on texture perception and identify any noise-related artifacts.
To ensure the fins are distinct entities and not fused with the background or the holder's hands.

Anatomical integrity of pectoral fin attachments
Correct asymmetry of the caudal fin
Boundary separation between shark and human hands
